current_answer: Azure now adds two distinct verified routes: eligible full-time university students can receive USD 100 for up to 12 months, while a new Azure customer can receive USD 1,000 instantly through Azure for Startups and may reach USD 5,000 after business verification. The startup route has a 90-day initial clock and 180 days after verification, so its higher number is not a longer runway. Vercel remains the verified funded, partner-gated route up to USD 30,000; NLnet remains the constrained individual open-technology grant route; Cloudflare Tier 3 remains unresolved for fully self-funded applicants.

catalogue_card.question: Before you take Azure’s USD 1,000 startup credit, can you use it in 90 days?
catalogue_card.text: Azure shows a USD 1,000 new-startup route with a 90-day clock and up to USD 5,000 after business verification. Eligible students get a separate USD 100 route over 12 months. Same provider, different decision.

summary: Individuals: Azure for Students offers eligible full-time university students USD 100 in credit within 12 months, without a card at sign-up.
Pre-funded startups: Azure for Startups shows USD 1,000 instantly for a new Azure customer and up to USD 5,000 after business verification.
The initial startup credit lasts 90 days; post-verification credit lasts 180 days, and pay-as-you-go follows expiry or use.
Funded startups: Vercel remains partner-gated and partner-specific up to USD 30,000, with a one-year-or-use limit and standard billing afterwards.
Cloudflare Tier 3 still pairs self-funded wording with a general recent-funding requirement; that conflict remains unresolved.
uncertainty: Azure for Startups country coverage, detailed business-verification rules, and full eligible-service list are not established by the reviewed comparison.
Azure for Students is a constrained student route, not evidence of worldwide individual-credit coverage.
One verified open-technology grant does not establish global individual-grant coverage.
Cloudflare has not published an explanation reconciling its self-funded Tier 3 wording with its general recent-funding requirement.
Unchanged AWS, Google, and Microsoft rows should be rechecked immediately before applying.
